# dsh-open-folder-visible

Windows fix for DSH: makes the Session-header **"open workspace in File Explorer"**
action raise a *

H: makes the Session-header **"open workspace in File Explorer"**
action raise a **visible** window.
## The problem

The Session header has an "Open In…" split button whose default action opens the
session's workspace
directory in File Explorer (also bound to `Ctrl+Alt+O`).

On Windows, clicking it starts Explorer, creates the correct directory window —
and that window is *

*invisible**. The button settles back to idle and reports
nothing, so the click looks like it did no

The button settles back to idle and reports
nothing, so the click looks like it did nothing at all.
### Why

The shipped `explorer` catalog entry in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-open-in-app` is
`kind: 'shell-open'`,
which on Windows ends at `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`windowsHide: true` exists to suppress the transient console window a CLI child
would flash. Applied

to Explorer it means the window is created with
`IsWindowVisible()` false.

Upstream judges the launch by exit code alone, and Explorer's exit 1 counts as a
delegated handoff (

`runExplorer`), so the route answers `{ ok: true }` whether or
not a window ever became visible.

## The fix

The Host half adds one route, `POST /open-folder-visible/open`, that spawns the
same `explorer.exe`

with `windowsHide: false`. Everything else mirrors the
shipped opener: an argv array (never a shell

string), Explorer's exit 1 accepted
as a delegated handoff, and a watch window so a launcher still r

unning is counted
as launched rather than killed.

The browser half wraps `globalThis.fetch` and reroutes **only** the file-manager
launch to that rout

e. Everything else — every other application, every other
request on the page — is passed through un

thing else — every other application, every other
request on the page — is passed through untouched.
### What this deliberately does not do

It does **not** replace the split button. The shipped button, its application
menu, its icons, its p

er-gesture feedback and the `Ctrl+Alt+O` shortcut
(`workspace.openLocal`) all stay exactly as they a

re. Replacing the component
would mean re-registering that shortcut, and forgetting to is how a "fix

" ends up
removing the hotkey.

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `launchWatchMs` | `1500` | Early-failure watch window
for the `explorer.exe` handoff. Launch success is decoupled from process exit, because Explorer exi
ts as soon as it has asked the running shell to raise the window. |
## Known limitations

- **Windows only.** On other platforms the route answers `501`; nothing else
changes.
- **This fixes

the workspace-open action only.** The file-location action
("reveal in File Explorer", `explorer.ex

e /select,<file>`, used by the
delivered-file cards and the changed-files review) is affected by the

same
`windowsHide` flag through a different code path
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller` →

`revealNativePath`), and is **not**
covered here.
- It reroutes one request by wrapping `globalThis.

fetch`. If a future release
changes the shipped launch route or the request body shape, the reroute

simply
stops matching and the shipped behaviour returns — the wrapper never breaks the
original requ
